entries.evidence: Raw usability test 2026-02-03 (research/raw/2026-02-03-usability-test-compass-ai-practice-setup-flow/session-notes.md, moderated think-aloud usability test, `:28`): `:53` "3 of 4 Practice Administrators (P154, P156, P157) hesitated at Invite your team. They weren't sure whether the email goes out when they finish the step or at Review & finish, and they didn't want staff emailed before champion training is booked for the practice. P155 entered the test staff list and went on without comment." P157 (`:64-65`): "If forty people get an email before anyone's booked training, my phone rings all afternoon." When this build actually sends the email isn't recorded ("The step 4 screen doesn't say when the invite email is sent, and these notes don't record when this build sends it", `:46-47`; open question `:84`), so a correct answer gives it as their uncertainty, not as fact. finding:compass-ai-practice-setup (`:72-75`), the topline (`:45-47`), the readout (`:102-105`), the persona (`:43-46`), the journey map (`:52-55`), the mental model (`:71-74`) and the storyboard (`:52-54`) restate the same 3 of 4. The worry is in this session only: the 2026-01-20 dashboard review records where setups stopped, not why (research/raw/2026-01-20-dashboard-review-compass-ai-practice-setup-completion/session-notes.md:72-74), and the 2026-02-24 IT Administrator interview has no invite-timing worry (its only invite item is provisioning, `:45`). entries.evidence: Every step is required. Raw dashboard review 2026-01-20 (research/raw/2026-01-20-dashboard-review-compass-ai-practice-setup-completion/session-notes.md, manual dashboard review, no participants, `:27`, `:62`): `:34-35` "Every step is required in this build; a setup can't skip a step, it can only be left open at it." Required because it is the only raw record that says every step is required. Raw usability test 2026-02-03 (research/raw/2026-02-03-usability-test-compass-ai-practice-setup-flow/session-notes.md): `:36-37` "Steps 3 and 4 are required in this build. There is no "Connect later" and no "Skip for now"; the only way past each step is to complete it." (steps 3 and 4 only). The five-step user flow quotes both (`:29-32`); finding:compass-ai-practice-setup: "five steps, all required in the build studied" (`:37`); the readout (`:27`) and the funnel summary (`:13`): "where every step is required". The topline (`:66`, "The calendar step is required") and the wireflow (`:59-61`, no skip branch on Connect calendar) state the calendar step only. Every "Connect later" and "Skip for now" in the corpus is inside a negation, so the must-not mustn't fire on one. Limit: the every-step statement comes from a dashboard review with no participants, describing the build; no session watched anyone try to skip a step. The old Basics/Signup, step-4-required and "all other steps required" must-nots are removed: those step names are retired, and step 4 and every other step are now required.

entries.evidence: Raw contextual inquiry 2026-02-17 (research/raw/2026-02-17-session-lock-during-dictation/session-notes.md, shadowing, researcher Priya Patel, `:34`): Method `:31-33` "Contextual inquiry / shadowing, 5 clinicians observed through at least one natural idle-timeout event during a real or simulated dictation session, plus 1 IT Security stakeholder interviewed on the technical constraints"; Key Findings `:38-41` "a session lock mid-recording simply freezes the ambient-scribe widget with no message; 4 of 5 clinicians assumed the draft was lost and started re-dictating from scratch after re-authenticating, even though the draft is server-side and actually survives the lock." participants.md: "**Count:** 5" (`:21`) and "4 clinicians recruited from regular ambient-scribe users on units with known short idle-timeout windows; 1 IT Security stakeholder recruited directly for technical context rather than shadowed." (`:30-32`). correction-2026-09-27.md, Participant count (`:36-38`): "5 participants in total, made up of 4 clinicians who were shadowed and 1 IT Security stakeholder who was interviewed but not shadowed. The session notes counted the IT Security stakeholder as a fifth clinician."; Draft-loss result (`:41-43`): "Only the 4 shadowed clinicians went through a lock during dictation, so this means **all 4 clinicians** assumed the draft was lost and started dictating again after they re-authenticated." finding:ambient-scribe-post-ga-refinements (`:42-43`): "all 4 shadowed clinicians assumed a locked session had destroyed their draft"; user-flows/ambient-scribe-session-lock-recovery (`:38-40`): "all 4 observed clinicians misread as data loss" (citing the correction); raw 2026-04-28 nurse practitioner interview (`:22`): "all 4 shadowed clinicians assumed the draft was lost". The trap: the raw note still reads "4 of 5" and "5 clinicians" (raw/ is append-only; the correction sits beside it), so an answer that cites the required raw record can still give the uncorrected count. The participant count is 5, but only the 4 clinicians were shadowed; the fifth was the IT Security stakeholder, who was interviewed, not shadowed, and never went through a lock. Required raw is 2026-02-17 because it is the only raw record that observed the lock, and it carries both the uncorrected note and the correction. The must-not on "4 of 5" is sentence-scoped: an answer may mention the original figure when the same sentence frames it as uncorrected. correction-2026-10-13.md (P31 is really P119) doesn't bear on the count. Limits: one session, one researcher, 4 shadowed clinicians, observed "during a real or simulated dictation session" (`:32`), so whether each lock was real isn't recorded; the re-test after the paused state ships (`:78-79`) hasn't happened.

entries.evidence: Raw survey 2025-09-09 (research/raw/2025-09-09-survey-clinician-burnout-documentation-burden-baseline/session-notes.md, survey, attitudinal): "Documentation burden ranked as the #1 self-selected contributor to burnout among physicians specifically (52%)"; "64% of physician respondents report regularly completing documentation after clinic hours ('pajama time'), averaging a self-reported 1.2 hours/day"; P84: "I do not love finishing my notes at 9pm"; P91: "don't let 'AI will fix documentation' become the excuse to skip fixing the actual EHR problems". Its own caveat: respondents were told the survey related to an AI initiative. Raw contextual inquiry 2025-04-22 (research/raw/2025-04-22-contextual-inquiry-ed-intake-shadowing/session-notes.md, behavioral): P23 "stop making me type the same sixteen fields". Raw nursing survey 2025-02-11: P41 "if it got me out of the room 10 minutes faster to chart" (its top concern, narrative voice, is about AI, not documentation pain). finding:clinician-experience-documentation-burden repeats the burnout survey. The burnout survey is required because it is the only raw record about documentation burden across clinicians. Coverage report (2026-09-29): the pipeline cited it but only repeated the burnout statistics, and the ED intake inquiry didn't reach the model. The chart-review inquiry (2025-01-29) is not a supporting record: its "cross-reference 3-4 systems" and "8-14 minutes per patient" chart review are care coordinators' pain before outreach calls, not documentation pain.

entries.evidence: Mockup mockups/confidence-highlighted-draft-review.md `:14`: "illustrative (the treatment in Notes beyond the underline itself is the designer's spec, not recorded in the test)". `:30-34`: "The 2026-01-13 session notes record only that low-confidence transcription was shown in a subtle underline (`:30`). The rest is the designer's spec and wasn't recorded in the test: high-confidence lines render as default text with no marking (deliberately inviting skimming), low-confidence lines also get an on-hover explanation, and there is no separate medium-confidence tier." `:23-27`: four later interviews say "the underline marks only where the scribe was unsure what it heard, so problems in lines it heard clearly aren't underlined". Raw usability test 2026-01-13 (research/raw/2026-01-13-usability-test-ambient-scribe-ga-release-candidate/session-notes.md) `:30`: "The new per-line confidence highlighting (low-confidence transcription shown in a subtle underline) was well received and, notably, 4 of 6 participants said it let them skim high-confidence lines for the first time across the whole testing history — the first session where reduced line-by-line reading was observed." `:43`: "the confidence-indicator concept appears to be the trust-building lever the team was looking for since September." Later raws, each one clinician's account: 2026-03-19 `:32` ("Incidental content is usually transcribed accurately, so it is not underlined"), 2026-06-30 `:31` ("Those lines are usually not underlined, because each word was heard clearly"), 2026-07-28 `:29` ("These lines are usually not underlined, because the words were heard clearly"), 2026-09-22 `:31` (same).
